# Translate, enforce terminology, publish

Translate content, enforce terminology, and round-trip the result back into its
original format with the local `kapi` CLI. For ongoing work, bind the locales,
voice profile, and terms in a project first — see [project.md](project.md).

## First decide: one-off file, or a project?

**A single file you just need translated** — a document, a deck, one catalog —
translate it directly. There is nothing to set up, and **do not run `kapi extract`**
(that reads a *project's* content config; on a loose file it fails with "no .kapi
project found"). Just round-trip it:

```bash
kapi pseudo-translate <file> --target-lang qps        # quick readiness pre-flight
kapi translate <file> --target-lang <lang> -o <out>  # reads the format, translates, writes it back
```

kapi preserves structure, tags, and placeholders (round-trip). Add `--credential
<name>` when it needs a model provider. That's the whole task for a one-off file.

# Android i18n — adoption playbook

Grades are the recommended-config Toil Index (see [../i18n.md](../i18n.md);
scores in [frameworks.yaml](frameworks.yaml)).

**`res/values/strings.xml` is the only option — T2 (recommended).** There is
no alternative string system on Android; the decision space is *around* it:
lint enforcement, per-app language, packaging filters, and the translation
pipeline. Stock it sits at S2/R2 (manual key lifecycle, runtime-only failure
discovery); the recommended config below buys it down to T2's best case.

## strings.xml — T2 (recommended; the only option)

Materialize target-language files for a project, or apply bilingual files
returned by a translator back onto the project's source locales.

With no -i in a project, merge writes the target-language files from the
project block store: a process-only "kapi run" (in a project, no -o)
commits its work as targets/<locale> overlays, and merge is the matching
sink — it reads each source, applies the stored overlays, and writes the
target-language file via the source format's skeleton round-trip.

With -i, merge applies one or more bilingual files returned by a
translator back onto the project's source locales, using the skeleton
captured by kapi extract. Each input carries the extraction
batch id in a file-level <note>, so merge finds the right extraction
manifest without guessing from the filename. Mixed target locales in one
batch are fine — merge handles each input independently.

Usage:
  kapi merge [flags]

Examples:
  kapi merge                     # materialize target-language files from the project store
  kapi merge -i out/app.en-to-fr.xliff
  kapi merge -i file1.xliff -i file2.xliff
  kapi merge -i vendor-return/ --no-memory-update

events.text:
The app is localized into French and the ship gate passes clean.

## What changed

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `app/src/main/res/values-fr/strings.xml` | **New** — French catalog, generated via kapi's round-trip |
| `app/src/main/res/values/donottranslate.xml` | **New** — holds `app_name` (brand, `translatable="false"`) |
| `app/src/main/res/values/strings.xml` | `app_name` moved out; now only translatable strings |
| `kapi.yaml`, `.kapi/` | **New** — project binding en→fr, the Android collection, and content memory |

```xml
<!-- values-fr/strings.xml -->
<string name="sign_in">Connectez-vous à votre espace de travail</string>
<string name="dashboard">Tableau de bord</string>
```

## How it was produced

Pre-flight with `kapi pseudo-translate --format androidxml` confirmed all strings were extractable, then `extract → translate → merge` so placeholders, escaping, and XML structure stayed under kapi's guardrails rather than being hand-edited. `kapi check --ship` → `pass: true`, QA gate, 0 findings.

`--format androidxml` is mandatory here — `.xml` is a shared extension, so kapi never infers it from the filename.

## Two judgment calls worth flagging

**`Northwind` is not translated** — it's a product name. I marked it `translatable="false"`, which kapi honored (the unit came out `translate="no"` and was excluded from the batch).

**Why the separate `donottranslate.xml`:** with `app_name` still in `strings.xml`, kapi's skeleton round-trip copied it into `values-fr/` verbatim, which trips Android lint's `ExtraTranslation` ("marked non-translatable but translated in locale fr"). kapi's writer has no flag to omit those units, so I used the standard Android convention instead. `R.string.app_name` resolves exactly as before — all `values/*.xml` are merged at build time — so there's no code impact.

## Recommended next, not applied

Your `build.gradle` has no lint config, so missing translations will silently fall back to English at runtime and only surface in QA. The Android playbook's fix:

```groovy
android { lint { error += ["HardcodedText", "MissingTranslation"] } }
```

Worth pairing with `androidResources { generateLocaleConfig = true }` for the API 33+ per-app language picker. I left `build.gradle` untouched since changing build failure behavior is your call — say the word and I'll add it.

One caveat on coverage: this repo has no Kotlin/Java source, only `build.gradle` and the catalog. Once real UI code lands, hardcoded literals in Compose (`Text("Hello")`) compile and ship untranslated with nothing catching them by default — that's exactly what the `HardcodedText` lint above is for.

To add a locale later: add it to `target_languages` in `kapi.yaml`, then `kapi extract --target-lang <lang> -p kapi.yaml`. The two French strings are in content memory, so re-runs prefill as exact matches.
I'll start by exploring the project structure to understand what we're working with.

Done. Both files are valid UTF-8 XML with correct key parity.

**Added `app/src/main/res/values-fr/strings.xml`:**

| Key | English | French |
|---|---|---|
| `sign_in` | Sign in to your workspace | Connectez-vous à votre espace de travail |
| `dashboard` | Dashboard | Tableau de bord |

**Changed `app/src/main/res/values/strings.xml`:** marked `app_name` as `translatable="false"`. "Northwind" is a brand name and shouldn't be translated — the attribute makes that omission deliberate and stops Android Lint from flagging it as `MissingTranslation`.

Translation notes:
- Used the formal *vous* register ("Connectez-vous"), which is the convention for French app UI.
- "Tableau de bord" is the standard French term for a dashboard.
- Neither string contains an apostrophe. Worth remembering for future French strings: a literal `'` in Android XML must be escaped as `\'` or the whole value wrapped in double quotes, otherwise the build fails.

Two things I did **not** do, since the project is a skeleton with no place to wire them:
- **No `res/xml/locales_config.xml`.** Per-app language preferences on Android 13+ need this file referenced via `android:localeConfig` in the manifest — and there's no `AndroidManifest.xml` here, so the file would be dangling. Worth adding once a manifest exists.
- **No `resConfigs`/`androidResources.localeFilters` in `build.gradle`.** The build file only declares `namespace` and `compileSdk`, with no `defaultConfig` block. French resources are picked up automatically by locale matching, so nothing is required for this to work.
